result.title: Trait Hitchhiking in LLM Post-Training
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is now a standard stage of language model post-training, and the compute devoted to it is growing rapidly. While it has been shown to improve capabilities, particularly for tasks with verifiable rewards, it can also change behaviours and internal properties that the reward does not explicitly target. We present a formalism to describe the evolution of "traits" during RL post-training and, in doing so, recover the Price equation from evolutionary biology. We use this to develop a mathematical model for what we call "trait hitchhiking": the amplification or suppression of non-targeted traits as training redistributes probability across completions. We evaluate this Price update expression on language models trained with GRPO and show that the Price estimates closely track the sampled trait dynamics. These results identify trait hitchhiking as a mechanism by which RL post-training can silently amplify undesirable traits.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出刻画 RL 后训练中「性状」演化的形式化框架，借入进化生物学的 Price 方程，建立「性状搭便车」模型来解释非目标性状如何随概率重新分配而被放大或抑制，并在 GRPO 训练的模型上检验 Price 估计能贴近采样到的性状动态。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把训练更新分解为选择与传递项的分析工具，可能可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中未被奖励直接监督的 latent 状态或行为如何被顺带强化，与贡献分配和训练副作用诊断相关；但论文为纯文本 RL，迁移可行性需进一步确认。
